title: Retain uncached block-map view after bounded consumer audit

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Audit CompiledRelationBlocks.block_map and current canonical Tensor/Fourfold consumers for repeated MappingProxyType(dict(self.blocks)) materialization. Prefer one local binding in bounded consumers. Do not add a cached second mapping, tuple-backed Mapping type, registry, alternate receipt family, backend or second compiler merely to eliminate theoretical repeated property access.

audit.owner_behavior: Each property access returns MappingProxyType(dict(self.blocks)); therefore a consumer that accesses block_map repeatedly rebuilds the same bounded name-to-block dictionary each time.

production_compatibility_consumer.finding: The compatibility facade requests exactly one explicit signature and returns compiled.blocks[0][1]; it does not materialize block_map.

relation_cost_probe.finding: The measured two-signature CSR constructor binds block_map exactly once and performs both exact-name lookups through that one immutable view.

heldout_csr_probe.finding: The measured four-signature CSR constructor binds block_map exactly once and performs all four exact-name lookups through that one immutable view.

contract_tests.finding: A small number of assertion-only tests access compiled.block_map more than once in one test body. They are not production or measured benchmark consumers and do not justify adding a persistent second representation to every receipt. Cosmetic local bindings would reduce only test allocation while adding churn, so they are intentionally left explicit for now.

audit.conclusion: No canonical production or measured diagnostic consumer currently rematerializes block_map in a repeated lookup loop. The existing bounded local-binding pattern already contains the allocation where it matters. Changing the receipt owner would either cache a second name map or introduce another Mapping abstraction, violating the Gardener preference for deletion/consolidation before abstraction without evidence of a real consumer problem.

decision.summary: Keep CompiledRelationBlocks.block_map as an uncached immutable view and keep binding it once in bounded multi-lookup consumers. Do not persist a duplicate mapping or create a new collection abstraction without a demonstrated repeated-access production consumer.

semantic_invariants.exact_lookup: Block lookup remains keyed by relation_block_name with exact string identity.
semantic_invariants.deterministic_order: CompiledRelationBlocks.blocks remains the canonical deterministic name-sorted immutable sequence.
semantic_invariants.direct_constructor_validation: Direct CompiledRelationBlocks construction continues to validate bounded sequence shape, duplicate names, TypedRelationBlock values, subject/semiring binding, signature-name agreement and semantic_fact_count.
semantic_invariants.source_of_truth: KnowledgeForest and FourfoldSnapshot remain authoritative; CompiledRelationBlocks and block_map remain regenerable computational views.
semantic_invariants.public_api: No public API, wire schema, benchmark schema, compatibility facade, promotion or authority contract changes.

result.summary: The bounded consumer audit found no measured or production multi-lookup path that repeatedly rebuilds block_map. The existing one-local-binding pattern is already used by both CSR probes, while the single-relation compatibility facade uses the canonical ordered blocks tuple directly. No executable change is justified.

verification.focused_static_audit: Verified current owner plus production compatibility facade and both measured CSR consumers on the exact base head. The two measured multi-lookup consumers each bind block_map once.
verification.ci_requirement: A documentation-only closure commit still requires exact-head workflow evidence before any green-PR claim; no pre-closure success is inferred.

bounded_next_step: GPU-86 only: audit the canonical compile_relation_blocks -> CompiledRelationBlocks handoff for duplicated semantic_fact_count traversal. Determine whether the compiler-side count and direct-constructor validation can share one already-required bounded pass without weakening direct-constructor validation, changing receipt fields, adding lazy state/cache, or creating a second receipt/compiler path. If not, retain the duplicate validation scan as the minimal receipt boundary.
